561befe92cefc825dc99ff893a8edde3b50691a0: The Encamp ski area, with its 215 km of runs, offers a fine range for all types of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 74 lifts make it possible to chain descents together without long waits. Encamp's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2640 m and a village at 1300 m, Encamp's snow cover is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters may cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly with the first significant snowfalls. The budget for a stay in Encamp is clearly high: 69€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Encamp is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It is hard to have a bad stay here.

56b955c38effc58c8a1c9032d705f8225b95ace0: Brambrüesch is a low-key, modest-sized resort — 20 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come to find calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Brambrüesch's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Brambrüesch's altitude (1170 m at the bottom, 2174 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The 49€ day lift pass places Brambrüesch among the intermediate resorts on budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Brambrüesch does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
